domain.text: TypeScript CLI/gateway tooling for GitHub-based agent learning submissions (vmethod): fork-sync avoidance and add-only learning-file policy

impressions.text: The domain is vmethod's CLI and gateway tooling for GitHub-based learning submissions: issue #51 records `learnings submit` failing with a 422 workflow-scope refusal once central changed `.github/workflows/`, and PR 52's task was to fix fork sync without ever requesting the workflow scope.

The codexbal/gpt-6.1-sol worker showed strong test discipline, reporting in round 1 that the old implementation failed 8 tests (8 failed / 19 passed) before the fix, that loud fakes reject forbidden requests, that disabling the stale guard made all 4 stale cases fail before restoration passed, and that format/lint/typecheck/all-tests/build/smoke/knip all exited 0.

The only round-1 review catch targeted the reviewer's own #51 spec rather than the worker's code, which the thread says followed the spec faithfully: the byte-identical fork/central precondition could never hold after the first merged submission, so changes were requested, the design became per-submission add-only files with central-authoritative novelty, and #51 was re-estimated from 2 to 5 points.

When the gateway returned no review content after the round-1 notification, the worker stopped and requested the authenticated amendment instead of guessing the new layout, and the orchestrator confirmed the first posting attempt had been refused by the closing-keyword guard and was reposted a minute later.

PR 52 merged the same day at 13 files (+770/−272) with 556 tests passing and `checks: green`, while the explicitly post-merge live acceptance (a fresh vmethod submission gaining the learning label with green CI) remained unclaimed by the worker because the label workflow runs `dev`'s code.

roundCauses.text: Round 1 changes were requested because of an explicitly self-identified flaw in the orchestrator's own #51 spec, not the implementation: the byte-identical fork/central precondition only holds until the first submission (#47) merges, after which later submissions would all fail since the fork cannot sync without the forbidden workflow scope, prompting the per-submission add-only redesign and the re-estimate of #51 from 2 to 5 points.

findings.text: The round-1 review was initially not readable through the gateway (`read-pr 52` returning only the task prompt, ACK and READY round 1), and the orchestrator stated the first review-post attempt was refused by the closing-keyword guard before being reposted a minute later.

Post-merge live acceptance cannot run before the merge because the label workflow runs `dev`'s code, so the fresh-submission acceptance (clean learning PR with central label and green CI) was explicitly left for the orchestrator and not claimed or attempted as a worker task.
